papers.title: A data-driven approach for learning traffic assignment using an artificial neural network
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Transport
papers.abstract: Solving transportation network design problems using traffic assignment models becomes increasingly impractical as the size of the considered network grows, due to the need to evaluate numerous candidate solutions. This study aims to model the traffic assignment process through a data-driven approach, and introduces a model based on an artificial neural network (ANN) to predict the total travel time in a network under various link capacity modifications for a specified set of links. ANN-based prediction models are trained and validated on a synthetic data set generated from a medium-sized network to evaluate the feasibility of the proposed approach. Models developed using different ANN architectures highlight the importance of selecting the most suitable architecture specific to the problem. The practical value of the ANN-based prediction model becomes apparent when used in optimising a transportation network design problem instead of the traditional traffic-assignment model: the ANN-based model reduced by up to 60 000 times the computation time required for the optimisation.

papers.title: Toward Lifecycle-Ready Digital Twins For Facility Technical Management
papers.abstract: Digital twins are increasingly promoted as a means to address persistent challenges in the built environment, yet their role in maintenance-focused facility management (FM) remains underexplored. This article explores the practical integration of digital twins into facility technical management through a real-life case environment involving three operational buildings and a two-year deployment period. Using a mixed-method approach combining surveys, interviews, operational observations, and industry feedback, the study investigates the organizational, technical, and information-management-related factors affecting the implementation and usability of BIM-based digital twins in maintenance operations.The findings identify key requirements related to BIM data structures, information management practices, naming conventions, and the involvement of maintenance stakeholders during the design and handover phases. Based on the case findings, the article outlines a four-step BIM process development framework and a four-step BIM enablement framework for facility technical management.The study further highlights the importance of user-friendly graphical user interfaces (GUIs) in bridging the gap between design-oriented BIM environments and the practical needs of maintenance personnel. The findings suggest that digital twins should be approached as continuously managed lifecycle information assets rather than static handover deliverables. The article contributes practice-oriented insights into how BIM-based digital twins can support information continuity and operational usability in facility technical management contexts.

papers.title: VirtuAI-Safe: Personalized Situated Safety Learning through Integration of VR and LLMs
papers.journal: Journal of Computing in Civil Engineering
papers.abstract: Abstract Construction safety outcomes are strongly shaped by human factors, including how individuals perceive hazards, interpret contextual cues, and make safety-related decisions in dynamic work environments. Safety education therefore plays a critical role in preparing future construction professionals to reason about risk and apply safety principles in context. Traditional safety instruction often emphasizes regulatory knowledge and procedural compliance, providing limited support for the development of judgment and decision-making skills required on real construction sites. This study examines a personalized situated learning approach for construction safety education that embeds instruction within realistic scenarios while supporting personalized learning. To examine this approach, which integrates virtual reality (VR) and large language models (LLMs), the study implemented VirtuAI-Safe, an immersive virtual learning environment designed to support context-aware and adaptive instructional guidance within simulated construction scenarios. In this study, VirtuAI-Safe is implemented as a construction safety education tool for undergraduate construction management students who are preparing for professional roles in the construction industry. Scaffolding safety was selected as the test domain because it represents a high-risk activity that requires interpretation of evolving site conditions and integration of multiple safety constraints. The system was evaluated using a single-group, postlearning assessment design with undergraduate construction management students. Learning outcomes were assessed using a knowledge test administered 2 days after a 1 h learning session, measuring factual, conceptual, procedural, and transfer knowledge. Learner engagement was measured immediately after the learning session across behavioral, cognitive, and affective dimensions. Overall, the results indicate that VirtuAI-Safe effectively supported learning and engagement within the scope of the study. Postlearning performance was strongest for conceptual understanding and knowledge transfer. Performance on factual and procedural knowledge showed greater variability following the delay, suggesting the need for reinforcement to sustain detailed recall and stepwise execution. Engagement results showed consistently strong behavioral and cognitive engagement, while affective engagement was more moderate. These findings suggest that personalized situated learning environments can support judgment-based aspects of construction safety education and inform future work on adaptive instructional support within immersive learning systems.

papers.title: Experimental assessment of engineering models with CFD derived heave hydrodynamic coefficients for a shallow draft barge-type floating wind turbine
papers.abstract: Nonlinear hydrodynamic loading for barge-type floating wind turbines (FWTs) remains particularly challenging to capture accurately using engineering (mid-fidelity) models. This study examines the wave-induced responses of a barge-type FWT. Model tests are performed for the novel WindBarge 16 MW FWT under various wave conditions. The heave added mass and quadratic damping are estimated using CFD simulations under forced oscillation in still water. Several engineering models are established using the aero-hydro-servo-elastic tool SIMA. The first-order and second-order difference-frequency wave loads are calculated based on potential flow theory. To account for viscous effects associated with the bilge keels around the platform bottom, CFD-derived added mass and quadratic damping/drag force formulations in heave are incorporated into the engineering model, while experimentally calibrated damping terms are included where needed. Numerical simulations are performed to reproduce the experiments under decay tests, regular and irregular waves. Platform motions and tower base fore-aft bending moments are compared against the experimental results. The CFD-derived heave added mass markedly improves the prediction of the natural period in heave (reducing the error compared to experiments from -9.61% to -3.93%) and the heave response in the wave-frequency range. Furthermore, the CFD-informed drag model improves the agreement with the measured heave response, as well as the pitch and tower-base bending moments near the natural frequency in pitch under irregular wave conditions. The experimental RAOs reveal wave-height-dependent nonlinear effects in surge, pitch, and tower-base bending moments, while the numerical models reproduce the overall response levels reasonably well but do not fully capture these trends.

papers.title: A Comparative Analysis of the Seismic Performance of Four Buildings Representative of Bagan’s Monumental Heritage
papers.abstract: This paper presents the outcomes of nonlinear static pushover and time history analyses, using both recorded and simulated ground motion signals, on 3D finite element macro-models of four buildings representative of Bagan’s monumental heritage: Myin-pya-gu (1493), Zan-thi (east) (558), Tha-mu-ti-hpaya (844), and Kya-zin-hpaya (1219). The simulations are validated against the observed seismic damage in the 1975 and 2016 earthquakes. The results of the nonlinear finite element method (NLFEM) analyses are complemented by seismic rocking analysis conducted on nonstructural elements, such as spires, through nonlinear kinematic analysis. Analytical estimates of acceleration levels capable of causing shear failure in spires are provided, focusing on elements with a slenderness ratio that makes them vulnerable to shearing rather than rocking (i.e. flexure-controlled) failure modes. A comparative assessment of seismic performance is presented for the four buildings, highlighting the influence of plan symmetry and vertical continuity. These attributes are proposed as key criteria for selecting appropriate retrofit schemes to protect Bagan’s monuments against future seismic events.

papers.title: Beam layout design in shear wall structures using a diffusion model guided by rule-based masks
papers.abstract: Serving as critical load supports and transfer components in shear wall structures, beams require layout designs that balance mechanical rationality with architectural functionality constraints. Conventional design methods, which rely on engineers' expertise, are challenging to systematize and are inherently inefficient. Moreover, existing intelligent design algorithms have attempted to integrate constraints related to architectural space and mechanical topology while delivering sufficiently detailed outputs, ultimately resulting in suboptimal outcomes. To address these challenges, this study synthesizes engineering experience rules pertaining to spatial functionality and load-bearing constraints and encodes them into a mask that delineates potential beam placement locations on a building plan. Subsequently, a diffusion model, well-known for its ability to generate intricate design details, is employed to produce the corresponding beam layout from the image mask. This approach, designated as the mask-constrained diffusion model for beam layout design in shear wall structures, introduces a key innovation: mitigating the uncontrolled generative range typically associated with diffusion models during beam layout configuration. By embedding engineering knowledge into a mask that constrains the diffusion process, the generation boundaries are effectively regulated, ensuring controllable and effective design outcomes. Analysis indicates that the designs produced by the mask-constrained diffusion model surpass the quality of existing intelligent design methods, achieving a relative 35.0% improvement in consistency with engineer-generated designs while concurrently satisfying critical mechanical performance criteria. This study provides a novel perspective on the intelligent design of beam layouts and serves as a valuable reference for the application of diffusion models in the structural design of buildings.

papers.title: Knowledge capabilities, knowledge processes, and perceived safety management practices in railway construction projects
papers.abstract: Railway construction relies on coordination across project organizations, yet evidence on how knowledge management relates to safety-management practices remains limited. This study examines associations among knowledge capabilities, knowledge processes and perceived safety-management practices in Thai railway projects. Questionnaire data were allocated chronologically to exploratory and confirmatory analyses (258 cases each). Principal-axis factoring (PAF) with Promax rotation, confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and structural equation modelling (SEM) were applied. Parallel analysis favored six knowledge factors, but the sixth factor had no dominant indicator in a matched solution; five factors were retained provisionally. The seven-factor, 42-indicator CFA yielded CFI)=)0.856 and RMSEA)=)0.069; the parsimonious SEM yielded CFI)=)0.846 and RMSEA)=)0.071. Nine of ten displayed direct paths and four aggregate indirect effects had bias-corrected bootstrap intervals excluding zero. Excluding an outcome item that explicitly invoked organizational knowledge removed bootstrap support for one path. The study offers a qualified capability-process-practice account for examining how project teams manage knowledge and reported safety routines. Construct overlap, modest model fit and self-reported outcomes limit inference; verified accident or injury reductions were not assessed.

papers.title: Delay-Compensated MPC for Path Tracking of Articulated Steering Vehicles
papers.journal: Journal of Transportation Engineering Part A Systems
papers.abstract: Abstract Articulated steering vehicles are key equipment for mining transportation, underground roadways, and heavy-duty material handling infrastructure, where insufficient path-tracking accuracy may reduce roadway safety margins and increase the risk of lane encroachment, collision, and traffic interruption in confined haulage corridors. Hydraulic actuator delay is a practical source of steering lag in such vehicles, but it is often simplified or neglected in existing path-tracking control studies. To address this gap, this study develops a delay-compensated model predictive control (MPC) framework by incorporating experimentally identified hydraulic actuator delay into the pre‍dictive control model. Simulation results showed that MPC provided better stability performance than linear quadratic regulator (LQR), reducing sideslip angle, yaw rate, and lateral acceleration by 21%–48% under representative lane-change maneuvers. With actuator-delay compensation, the proposed MPC further reduced the tractor lateral deviation by 53.12% under single lane change (SLC) and 83.63% under double lane change (DLC) conditions. These results indicate that the proposed method can improve the operational safety, tracking reliability, and automation readiness of articulated vehicles used in mining and infrastructure transportation scenarios.

papers.title: A generalized parameter calibration framework for typhoon wave models using pre-optimization dimensionality reduction in the South China Sea
papers.abstract: Accurate simulation of wave fields under extreme typhoon sea states is of great significance to ocean engineering and disaster prevention and mitigation. However, third-generation wave models still exhibit considerable uncertainty under strong wind conditions, and their empirical parameters lack systematic calibration. Targeting the South China Sea (SCS) as the study area, this paper proposes an automated parameter calibration framework based on “Morris global sensitivity analysis and Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) Bayesian optimization” utilizing the ST6 source term package of the WAVEWATCH III (WW3) model. First, a sensitivity analysis is conducted on nine key physical parameters, identifying CDFAC, SINWS, SINA0, SWLB1, and GAMMA as the dominant parameters. Subsequently, aimed at multi-typhoon joint calibration (Kompasu, Maon), an objective function is constructed based on the mean root mean square error (RMSE) from 10 typhoon buoy samples, and 200 optimization iterations are performed. The results indicate that the optimal parameter combination reduces the mean RMSE of the calibration set from 0.5167 m to 0.3800 m, an improvement of 26.5%, yielding a parameter combination significantly superior to the default configuration for the SCS. Validated by four independent typhoons (Nesat, Mangkhut, Molave, Saudel) involving 17 typhoon buoy samples, the independent validation set showed an improvement of 29.69% in the mean RMSE and an approximately 61.86% reduction in the mean absolute Bias, which verifies its robustness and generalization capability. This study provides an efficient and transferable parameter calibration method, and the obtained optimal parameters demonstrate excellent applicability for typhoon wave simulations in the SCS.

papers.title: Dowel-bearing strength for engineered bamboo products: Review and data-driven analysis
papers.abstract: Engineered bamboo products, represented by laminated bamboo and bamboo scrimber, have attracted increasing attention in sustainable construction. Connections in engineered bamboo structures often rely on bolted joints, for which half-hole dowel-bearing strength is a key parameter for characterizing the local bearing response. This study reviewed the manufacturing processes of laminated bamboo and bamboo scrimber and summarized common testing methods for evaluating the dowel-bearing strength of engineered bamboo products. After introducing the failure modes of dowel-bearing test specimens, the primary influencing factors for dowel-bearing strength were discussed. Based on a database of 1634 half-hole specimens, dowel-bearing strength was predicted using a data-driven machine learning (ML) approach. A new theoretical model based on stress dispersion theory was developed, considering specimen dimensions, dowel diameter, and the corresponding material yield strength in compression. The coefficients in the developed theoretical model were determined using a combined algorithm in which the model was embedded into ML algorithms. It was found that, for specimens loaded parallel and perpendicular to the grain, the dowel significantly influenced a region extending up to 4.50 times its diameter along the corresponding dispersion angle; for specimens loaded parallel to the grain, within the theoretical region of significant influence described above, the dowel also significantly affected a region within 0.45 times the specimen length along the corresponding dispersion angle. The predictive performance of the proposed theoretical model was slightly lower than that of most of the data-driven ML models, but it markedly outperformed the models adopted in current design codes and offered good physical interpretability.

papers.title: IIGF-Net: An interpretability-driven intensity-geometry fusion framework for shield tunnel leakage segmentation in 3D point clouds
papers.abstract: Automated leakage detection from MLS-acquired 3D point clouds is essential for the preventive maintenance of shield tunnels. However, existing deep learning methods must reconcile the use of physically grounded handcrafted descriptors with the opaque representations learned by high-capacity networks. Without a principled means to verify whether handcrafted descriptors are effectively utilized by the trained network, descriptor design remains heuristic and the integration of domain knowledge with deep learning remains unverified. This study proposes an interpretability-driven intensity-geometry fusion network (IIGF-Net) for binary leakage segmentation in static point clouds. The framework combines nine multiscale geometric descriptors, a Fused Intensity Descriptor (FID), a two-level descriptor verification procedure, and Graph Boundary-Aware Loss (GBALoss). The verification procedure uses Gradient × Input attribution and exhaustive channel-zeroing screening across all 512 combinations of the nine geometric descriptors, followed by retraining of selected configurations to calibrate the effects of feature removal. GBALoss uses k −nearest-neighbor label relationships to emphasize leakage-background boundary points during optimization. Using an adopted DeepGCN backbone without external pretraining, IIGF-Net achieved an IoU_leakage of 87.32 ± 0.34% and an mIoU of 93.39 ± 0.17% over five runs on the validation set. IoU_leakage remained above 81% on three independent test sets. Under the tested retraining configuration, a six-descriptor subset achieved an IoU_leakage of 86.90%, compared with 87.32% for the full descriptor configuration. GBALoss increased the boundary F1-score from 72.22% to 78.47%. These results support descriptor verification as a practical basis for feature selection and indicate that the proposed components improve leakage segmentation within the evaluated tunnel datasets.
